Rashi on Ketubot 63a:1:1.english: You are conducting yourself - You conduct yourself.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:1:3.english: Mine and yours is hers - The Torah that I learned and that you learned is through her.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:3:1.hebrew: שקל מנא - כלי זיין, כאילו בא להלחם:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:3:1.english: He took a vessel - A weapon, as if he were coming to fight.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:3:2.english: They were preoccupied - with that quarrel.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:3:3.hebrew: לא מר איפסיק ולא מר איפסיק - לא אכלו סעודת יום הכפורים שמפסיקין בה אכילה להתענות. סעודה אחרונה של ערב ט' באב ויוה"כ קרי סעודה המפסקת, שמפסיקים בה, במס' תענית (דף ל.):
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:3:3.english: Neither this Master ceased [eating], nor did that Master cease [eating] - They did not eat the Yom Kippur meal with which one ceases eating in order to fast. The final meal on the eve of Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur is called se'udah hamafseket [the concluding meal], with which one ceases [eating], in Tractate Ta'anit (30a).

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:4:1.hebrew: המורדת על בעלה - בגמ' מפרש ממאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:4:1.english: Who rebels against her husband - In the Gemara, it explains from what [she rebels].

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:4:3.hebrew: עד כדי כתובתה - ואחר כך נותן לה גט ויוצאה בלא כתובה, אבל אינו משהה לפסוק על הנכסים שנפלו לה מבית אביה ולהפסידה ממנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:4:3.english: Up to the amount of her marriage contract - And afterward he gives her a bill of divorce and she leaves without [receiving] her marriage contract, but he does not delay [divorcing her] to assess [further deductions] against the property that fell to her from her father's house and cause her to lose [any] of it.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:4:4.english: Three dinars - In the Gemara it explains what the difference is between him and her.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:5:1.english: Where he says, "I will not sustain" - For that is in place of [her] labor.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:6:1.hebrew: והאמר רב יוציא - ומתניתין מוסיפין תנן, ואינו מוציא לאלתר:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:6:1.english: But didn't Rav say [that] he must divorce [her] - Yet [in] our Mishnah we learned "they add," and he does not divorce [her] immediately.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:6:2.hebrew: ולאו אימלוכי ביה בעי - שמא יחזור בו, ובתוך זמן שאנו נמלכין בו ומחזירין עליו שיחזור בו, מוסיפין על כתובתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:6:2.english: And doesn't he need to be consulted? - Perhaps he will retract [his statement], and during the time that we consult with him and try to persuade him to retract [it], we add to her ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:7:1.hebrew: אחת לי - כולן שוות בתורת מרד, ואפילו שהיא נדה או חולה והיא מורדת:
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:7:1.english: It is the same to me - All of them are equal with respect to the law of rebellion, even when she is a menstruating woman or ill and she rebels.

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:7:2.hebrew: ארוסה - שאמרה לא אנשא: ה"ג: בשלמא למ"ד מתשמיש, שפיר; אלא למ"ד משום מלאכה, חולה בת מלאכה היא? בשלמא למ"ד מתשמיש, שפיר, ואי משום נדה דלאו בת תשמיש היא — אינו דומה מי שיש לו פת בסלו כו' כדלקמן; אלא למאן דאמר כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:7:2.english: A betrothed woman - Who said, "I will not be married." This is how we read [the Gemara]: "Granted, according to the one who says [that her rebellion is] from marital relations, it is well; but according to the one who says [it is] because of work, is an ill woman fit for work?" Granted, according to the one who says [it is] from marital relations, it is well — and if [you ask] concerning a menstruating woman, who is not fit for marital relations, [the answer is:] one who has bread in his basket is not comparable [to one who does not], etc., as [stated] below — but according to the one who says [it is because of work], etc.:

Rashi on Ketubot 63a:9:1.hebrew: ה"ג: בשלמא למ"ד מתשמיש שפיר, אלא למ"ד משום מלאכה, חולה בת מלאכה היא - בשלמא למ"ד מתשמיש, שפיר; ואי משום נדה דלאו בת תשמיש היא, אינו דומה מי שיש לו פת בסלו כו', כדלקמן. אלא למאן דאמר כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 63a:9:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: Granted, according to the one who says [the Mishnah refers to] marital relations, [it is] well; but according to the one who says [it is] because of work, is an ill woman capable of work? - Granted, according to the one who says [it refers to] marital relations, [it is] well; and if [you ask] regarding a niddah [a menstruating woman], who is not fit for marital relations, [the answer is that] one who has bread in his basket is not comparable [to one who does not], etc., as [stated] below. But according to the one who says, etc.

Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:2:1.hebrew: אדעתא דגברא רבה מי נדרת - וא"ת: והלא אסור לפתוח בנולד, דאמרינן בנדרים בפ' ר' אליעזר (נדרים דף סד.): כיצד? אמר "קונם שאיני נהנה לפלוני" ונעשה סופר כו'! וי"ל, דהכא לא חשיב נולד כיון שהלך לבי רב, דדרך הוא בהולך ללמוד שנעשה אדם גדול. אי נמי, כגון דתלה נדרו בדבר, שפירש בשעה שנדר על דעת אם לא יעשה סופר, דבענין זה לא הוה נולד; כדתנן בפרק רבי אליעזר (נדרים דף סה.): "קונם שאיני נושא את פלונית שאביה רע, אמרו לו מת או עשה תשובה" כו', ופריך בגמ': מת — נולד הוא, וה"ה עשה תשובה! ומשני: אמר רב הונא, נעשה כתולה נדרו בדבר. ורבי יוחנן דמשני התם בענין אחר — לאו משום דפליג אתולה נדרו בדבר, אלא דלא חשיב ליה כתולה נדרו בדבר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:2:1.english: "Did you vow thinking [he would become] a great man?" - And if you ask: Is it not forbidden to use a newly arisen circumstance [nolad] as an opening [to nullify a vow], as we say in Nedarim in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer (Nedarim 64a): "How so? [If] one said, 'Konam that I will not benefit from so-and-so,' and he [later] became a scribe," etc.? And it can be answered that here it is not considered nolad since he went to the study hall, for it is the normal course for one who goes to study that he becomes a great man. Alternatively, [it is a case] where he made his vow dependent on a condition — that he specified at the time he vowed [that it was] on the condition that he not become a scribe — for in this manner it is not nolad; as we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer (Nedarim 65a): "'Konam that I will not marry so-and-so because her father is wicked'; they said to him, 'He died,' or 'He repented,'" etc., and [the Gemara] objects: "'He died' is nolad, and the same applies to 'He repented'!" And [the Gemara] answers: Rav Huna said, it becomes like one who makes his vow dependent on a condition. And Rabbi Yochanan, who answers there in a different manner — it is not because he disagrees regarding one who makes his vow dependent on a condition, rather because he does not consider it to be like one who makes his vow dependent on a condition.

Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:2:2.hebrew: ברתיה דר' עקיבא עבדא ליה לבן עזאי הכי - וא"ת: והא בפ' קמא דסוטה (דף ד:) פריך: "והא איכא בן עזאי דלא נסיב"? ולההוא לישנא דמשני "נסיב ופירש", אתי שפיר. ויש לומר, דאע"ג דקאמר הכא דעבדא הכי לבן עזאי, מ"מ לא נשאה אלא באירוסין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:2:2.english: Rabbi Akiva's daughter did the same for Ben Azzai - And if you will ask: But in the first chapter of Sotah (4b), [the Gemara] asks: "But there is Ben Azzai, who did not marry"? And according to that version that answers "he married and separated," it fits well. And one can say that even though it says here that she did thus for Ben Azzai, nevertheless he only married her through betrothal [and did not consummate the marriage].

Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:4:1.hebrew: פוחתין לה ז' דינרין - בירושלמי מפרש: כנגד שבע מלאכות שהאשה עושה לבעלה; וגבי המורד דמוסיפין שלשה דינרין, מפרש: כנגד שארה כסותה ועונתה. והש"ס שלנו אין סובר כן, דהא בעי בגמרא: "מה בין מורד למורדת", ומפרש טעמא אחרינא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:4:1.english: "Her [marriage contract] is reduced by seven dinars" - In the Yerushalmi it explains: [This is] corresponding to the seven labors that a wife performs for her husband; and regarding the rebellious [husband], where three dinars are added, it explains: [This is] corresponding to her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights. However, our Talmud does not hold like this, for behold, it asks in the Gemara: "What is the difference between a rebellious husband and a rebellious wife?" and it explains a different reason.

Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:5:2.hebrew: באומר איני זן ואיני מפרנס - מכאן מוכיח רבינו אליהו, שחייב אדם להשכיר עצמו ללמד תינוקת או לעשות מלאכה אחרת כדי לזון את אשתו, דאם לא כן, מה ענין זה אצל מורד ממלאכה? ומיהו בקונטרס פירש: משום דזן ומפרנס הוא כנגד מלאכה של אשה. ועוד הביא ראיה מדכתבינן בכתובה "ואנא אפלח" כו'. ומיהו גם זה יש לדחות, כמו שמפרש ר"ת, דאפלח היינו עבודת הקרקע — פירוש: אחרוש ואנכש ואעדור את השדה ואביא מזונות לבית — אבל להשכיר עצמו אינו חייב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:5:2.english: Where he says, "I will not sustain and I will not support" - From here Rabbeinu Eliyahu proves that a man is obligated to hire himself out to teach schoolchildren or to do other work in order to sustain his wife, for if not, what connection does this have to [one who] rebels against [performing] work? However, in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained [that it is] because "sustaining and supporting" corresponds to the work of a wife. And furthermore, [Rabbeinu Eliyahu] brought a proof from what we write in the ketubah: "And I will work [eflach]," etc. However, this too can be refuted, as Rabbeinu Tam explains, that eflach means working the land — meaning: I will plow, weed, and hoe the field and bring food to the house — but he is not obligated to hire himself out.

Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:6:1.hebrew: והאמר רב האומר איני זן ואיני מפרנס יוציא ויתן כתובה - משמואל, דפליג עליה דרב בסוף המדיר (לקמן כתובות דף עז.) דקאמר: "עד שכופין אותו להוציא יכפוהו לזון" — לא מצי למפרך, דלדידיה אתי שפיר, דאע"פ שכופין אותו על כרחו לזונה, מכל מקום מוסיפין, כיון דאינו רוצה לזונה אלא על ידי כפיה, דאין אדם דר עם נחש בכפיפה אחת; אבל לרב, שכופין אותו לגרשה מיד, מה שייך תוספת? ואם תאמר: למאן דאמר מתשמיש נמי תקשי, דעל כרחך מורד מתשמיש נמי כופין להוציא, דאטו לעולם יוסיפו על כתובתה ותתעגן כל ימיה? ויש לומר: דהוה מצי למימר "ולטעמיך":
Tosafot on Ketubot 63a:6:1.english: But didn't Rav say: One who says, "I will not sustain and I will not support" must divorce [her] and give [her] the ketubah - From Shmuel, who disagrees with Rav at the end of [chapter] Hamadir (below, Ketubot 77a) and says, "Rather than compelling him to divorce [her], let them compel him to sustain [her]," [the Gemara] could not ask [this question], for according to him it works out well: even though they compel him against his will to sustain her, nevertheless they add [to her ketubah], since he does not want to sustain her except through compulsion, for no person lives with a snake in one basket. But according to Rav, who [holds that] they compel him to divorce her immediately, what relevance does an addition [to the ketubah] have? And if you should ask: According to the one who says [that the Mishnah refers to rebellion] from marital relations, [this question] should also be difficult, for perforce [in the case of] one who rebels from marital relations they also compel [him] to divorce [her], for would they forever add to her ketubah while she remains chained [in marriage] all her days? And one can answer: [The Gemara] could have said, "And according to your own reasoning!"
